root_cause.text: The driver reads an untrusted 10-bit message size from the sink's RxStatus register and uses it as the read length for the ReceiverID list without clamping to the fixed buffer size (177 bytes), allowing a malicious HDMI repeater to cause an out-of-bounds write during I2C read.
root_cause.evidence: The patch clamps the read length using `MIN(hdcp->auth.msg.hdcp2.rx_id_list_size, sizeof(hdcp->auth.msg.hdcp2.rx_id_list))` in `mod_hdcp_read_rx_id_list()`, and the commit description explicitly states that the 10-bit message size (max 1023) is used without clamping to the destination buffer `rx_id_list[177]`.
